previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease, diabetes, coronary artery disease, and recent pacemaker explantation for enterococcal bacteremia presented with chest pain and bradycardia, leading to a brief pulseless electrical activity arrest in the emergency department. He was resuscitated with chest compressions and atropine, intubated, and admitted to the ICU. The arrest was likely due to vagal stimulation during central line placement. He underwent hemodialysis, which improved his mental status and metabolic parameters. His bradycardia resolved, and he was extubated on hospital day two. Fever and leukocytosis from prior bacteremia improved with continued vancomycin and gentamicin. Chest pain was attributed to resuscitation-related trauma. He was discharged home in stable condition on day four with instructions to complete his antibiotic course, follow up with cardiology, and monitor weight.
